bull_bear.body:
- Owns strategically located legacy land assets, including approximately 10 acres of Birla Mills land in Kamla Nagar, Delhi, allowing value to be unlocked through development and revenue-sharing arrangements
- Partnership with credible developers — Oro Bloom Developments Private Limited, a joint venture between the Hines Group and the Conscient Group — providing access to capital, technology, execution capability and market expertise while reducing development risk
- Recurring lease income base, with the Gurugram property fully leased out during the year
- Early-mover clean-energy asset: a 3 MW mini hydel plant that generated and evacuated 98.87 lakh units of green power during the year versus 80.25 lakh units in the previous year
- Conservative balance-sheet posture, with the Directors' Report noting a Debt Equity Ratio of 0.02 times
- Long corporate history — the 86th Annual Report — with a portfolio of subsidiaries and an associate whose performance the Board described as satisfactory
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Narrow and concentrated income base — The Company continues to derive its major income from leased properties, income from investment and operations of a single Mini Hydro Power Unit in Kalimpong District, West Bengal - a very small number of assets carries the earnings, so under-performance of any one of them has an outsized effect.
- Property demand, interest rate, construction cost and financing cycles — MD&A Threats/Risks: the real estate sector remains exposed to fluctuations in property demand, interest rates, construction costs and availability of financing.
- Input cost inflation eroding project viability and margins — MD&A Threats/Risks: rising land, labour and raw-material costs may adversely affect project viability and margins.
- Regulatory, land-use and approval risk — MD&A Threats/Risks: changes in government policies, land-use regulations, environmental norms, taxation and approval processes may result in delays and additional costs. The Birla Mills development is itself still progressing through statutory approvals and regulatory clearances.
- Competitive pressure on pricing and returns — MD&A Threats/Risks: increasing competition among developers, particularly in attractive urban locations, could exert pressure on pricing and returns.
- Dependence on a third-party development partner for value realisation — Value from the Birla Mills land is to be realised on a revenue-sharing basis through Oro Bloom Developments Private Limited; the timing and quantum of the Company's share depend on that partner's execution and on the approvals it is pursuing.
- Hydel project viability drivers — MD&A: project viability is highly dependent on water availability, PLF, tariff/PPA, project cost, evacuation infrastructure and timely regulatory approvals. The same variables govern the proposed 6 MW upstream expansion, which remains contingent on a feasibility decision after the Detailed Project Report.
- Thin organisational depth and key-personnel churn — The number of employees as at 31 March 2026 was 28, and the year saw several senior changes - a Non-Executive Director resigned w.e.f. 10 November 2025, the Company Secretary changed, a Managing Director was appointed w.e.f. 11 November 2025 and the Manager was redesignated as Business Head - concentrating execution capability in very few people.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.body:
- Unlock latent value embedded in the real estate portfolio through selective, high-quality development opportunities pursued via credible partnerships, with a focus on maximising long-term shareholder value from real estate assets
- Develop approximately 10 acres of the Birla Mills land at Kamla Nagar, Delhi on a revenue-sharing basis under a Joint Development Agreement with Oro Bloom Developments Private Limited, a joint venture between the Hines Group and the Conscient Group
- Phased development of the land bank alongside selective development partnerships, to generate capital appreciation as well as recurring income
- Enhance the renewable energy portfolio, with a Detailed Project Report initiated for an additional 6 MW hydel facility upstream of the existing Neora plant, to be implemented only after technical, financial and regulatory feasibility is evaluated
- Maintain lease-based recurring income from owned property, with the Gurugram property fully leased out during the year
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Expansion is concentrated in two areas. In real estate, the Company executed a Joint Development Agreement in January 2025 with Oro Bloom Developments Private Limited - a joint venture between the Hines Group and the Conscient Group - for the development of approximately 10 acres of the Birla Mills land at Kamla Nagar, Delhi, structured on a revenue-sharing basis; the development partner is currently progressing through the requisite statutory approvals and regulatory clearances in accordance with the agreed development plan and mutually established timelines, and no commissioning date is disclosed. In power, the Company operates a 3 MW Mini Hydel Power Plant at Neora, Kalimpong, West Bengal, which generated and evacuated 98.87 lakh units of green power during the year against 80.25 lakh units in the previous year; to further enhance its renewable energy portfolio it has initiated preparation of a Detailed Project Report for an additional 6 MW hydel power generation facility on the upstream stretch of the Neora River in close proximity to the existing plant, and will evaluate technical, financial and regulatory feasibility on completion of the DPR before deciding on implementation. Separately, the Company's property at Gurugram was fully leased out during the year. No usable rupee capex quantum is disclosed - the segment capital-expenditure figures supplied are tagged ambiguous with no printed unit.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The Indian real estate sector is expected to maintain a strong long-term growth trajectory, supported by rapid urbanisation, rising disposable incomes, infrastructure development and the expanding middle class
- The sector is emerging from a traditional land-and-construction-driven industry into a more technology-enabled, institutional and infrastructure-linked sector, with growth expected across residential, commercial, industrial, warehousing, logistics, data centres and integrated townships
- Expansion of Tier-II and Tier-III cities and development of new economic corridors are expected to further broaden the addressable market; increasing institutional participation, professionalisation and strategic partnerships are expected to strengthen the sector
- Overall the long-term real estate outlook remains positive, supported by India's economic growth and the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision
- Opportunities exist for landowners to unlock value from strategically located land assets through development, monetisation and revenue-sharing arrangements; strategic partnerships provide access to capital, technology, execution capabilities and market expertise while reducing development risks
- Rising demand for quality residential and commercial spaces, industrial and logistics parks, and data centres is expected to create new avenues for growth; technology adoption, sustainable development and green buildings can further enhance asset value and long-term competitiveness
- A 3 MW hydel project has a positive medium-to-long-term industry outlook, supported by India's renewable-energy transition and renewed government focus on small hydro, though viability is highly dependent on water availability, PLF, tariff/PPA, project cost, evacuation infrastructure and timely regulatory approvals
- Major income continues to be derived from leased properties, income from investment and operations of the Mini Hydro Power Unit in Kalimpong District, West Bengal
